findings.detail: spec-coverage.sh flags SPEC.md:156's (no-test: ...) waiver on this chain's own R-13 (manual real-vault verification) as stale because the literal text 'R-13' appears in test files the plan scopes in (e.g. UITests/WorkspaceOpenStateUITests.swift:111, a doc comment dated 2026-08-26, predating this Step 5 segment). That comment references an UNRELATED R-13 from a different plan's own requirement numbering (each plan restarts its own R-01.. sequence) - it is not automated coverage of THIS chain's R-13, which remains genuinely human-only (real iCloud vault, cannot run unattended). Did not apply the tool's suggested remedy (deleting the no-test clause) because doing so would falsely claim R-13 is now test-covered when it is not.

waiver_decision.decision: Waive as false positive. SPEC.md's (no-test: ...) clause for R-13 stays untouched.
waiver_decision.rationale: Checker does a plan-wide substring match on the ID text across every test file the plan scopes in, with no awareness that requirement IDs restart at R-01 per plan. The 'R-13' hit is an ID collision with an unrelated plan's own numbering, not a real coverage gap.

findings.detail: Same mechanism: SPEC.md:159's (no-test: ...) waiver on this chain's R-16 (scripts/uitests.sh must pass, human-run only per CLAUDE.md) is flagged stale because 'R-16' appears in UITests/WorkspaceIntegrationUITests.swift:3, a doc-comment header dated 2026-08-24 from a DIFFERENT chain's plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-24-workspace-tasks-notes-integration.md, Task 10), which has its own, unrelated R-16. This chain's own R-16 (the human-run scripts/uitests.sh gate) has not been run by me, deliberately, and the waiver should NOT be deleted.

waiver_decision.decision: Waive as false positive. SPEC.md's (no-test: ...) clause for R-16 stays untouched.
